Definition: of Hebrew origin (H5283); Neeman (i.e. Naaman), a Syrian:--Naaman.
BiblicalUsage: Naaman is the Syrian leper Jesus names in the synagogue at Nazareth, the one stranger cleansed in the days of Elisha when no leper in Israel was cleansed. Jesus holds him up as the proof that God's mercy reaches beyond Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Jesus names Naaman to sting His hearers: God's mercy reached the Syrian while Israel's lepers went unhealed, and the gospel has always gone where faith answers.
